name: Ganglioneuroblastoma

criteria.description: Presence of both neuroblastic (primitive neuroblasts) and ganglionic cells with Schwannian stroma
Positive staining for neuronal markers such as NSE, synaptophysin, and chromogranin
Identification of a heterogeneous mass with calcifications on CT or MRI in typical locations (adrenal gland, sympathetic chain)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of mixed neuroblastic and ganglionic cells with Schwannian stroma plus positive neuronal immunohistochemical markers
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Molecular genetic testing for MYCN amplification may aid prognosis but is not diagnostic.

pathognomonic.notes: Often firm and irregular, located in adrenal or paraspinal region
Ptosis, miosis, and anhidrosis due to cervical sympathetic chain involvement

common.notes: Due to mass effect or local invasion

common.symptomName: Weight loss and failure to thrive
searchTerms: failure to gain weight and lose weight

common.notes: Due to tumor infiltration or paraneoplastic effects

occasional.notes: Paraneoplastic syndrome associated with neuroblastoma family tumors
Due to vasoactive intestinal peptide secretion in rare cases

searchTerms: back pain with nerve compression signs
weakness or numbness from spinal cord squeezing
balance and movement problems from immune reaction

laboratory: Anemia and thrombocytopenia in advanced disease
imaging: CT or MRI showing heterogeneous adrenal or paraspinal mass with calcifications
MIBG scintigraphy positive for tumor localization
other: Histopathology showing mixed neuroblastic and ganglionic cells with Schwannian stroma
Immunohistochemistry positive for neuronal markers (NSE, synaptophysin, chromogranin)

distinguishingFeatures: Predominantly primitive neuroblasts without mature ganglion cells

redFlags: Neurological deficits indicating spinal cord compression
Signs of catecholamine crisis (hypertensive emergency, tachyarrhythmia)
references: Maris JM. Recent advances in neuroblastoma. N Engl J Med. 2010;362(23):2202-2211.
Brodeur GM, et al. International Neuroblastoma Pathology Classification: a consensus. Cancer. 1999;86(2):364-372.
London WB, et al. Clinical and biologic features predict outcome in ganglioneuroblastoma. J Clin Oncol. 2011;29(15):2086-2091.
